arxiv-2004-09437.title: A Normal Form for Two-Input Flat Nonlinear Discrete-Time Systems
arxiv-2004-09437.creator: Johannes Diwold, Bernd Kolar, Markus Schöberl
arxiv-2004-09437.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Johannes Diwold, Bernd Kolar, Markus Schöberl. We show that every flat nonlinear discrete-time system with two inputs can be transformed into a structurally flat normal form by state- and input transformations. This normal form has a triangular structure and allows to read off the flat output, as well as a systematic construction of the parameterization of all system variables by the flat output and its forward-shifts. For flat continuous-time systems no comparable normal form exist.

arxiv-2112-15586.title: Meson structure on the light-front III The Hamiltonian, heavy quarkonia, spin and orbit mixing
arxiv-2112-15586.creator: Edward Shuryak, Ismail Zahed
arxiv-2112-15586.description: Abstract This is the third paper on hadronic light front wave functions (LFWFs). We derive a light front Hamiltonian from first principles, using the key features of the QCD vacuum at low resolution. In the first approximation, it gives transverse oscillator and longitudinal harmonic modes, and yields the correct Regge trajectories.

Recommender systems that learn from implicit feedback often use large volumes of a single type of implicit user feedback, such as clicks, to enhance the prediction of sparse target behavior such as purchases. arxiv-2310-19308.title: Free from Bellman Completeness: Trajectory Stitching via Model-based Return-conditioned Supervised Learning
arxiv-2310-19308.creator: Zhaoyi Zhou, Chuning Zhu, Runlong Zhou, Qiwen Cui, Abhishek Gupta, Simon S. Du
arxiv-2310-19308.description: Abstract Off-policy dynamic programming (DP) techniques such as Q Q -learning have proven to be important in sequential decision-making problems. In the presence of function approximation, however, these techniques often diverge due to the absence of Bellman completeness in the function classes considered, a crucial condition for the success of DP-based methods.

arxiv-2401-04138.title: Expanding Horizons in HCI Research Through LLM-Driven Qualitative Analysis DOI: none CCS: Human-centered computing Human computer interaction (HCI) CCS: Human-centered computing HCI design and evaluation methods
arxiv-2401-04138.creator: Maya Grace Torii, Takahito Murakami, Yoichi Ochiai
arxiv-2401-04138.description: Abstract . How would research be like if we still needed to "send" papers typed with a typewriter? Our life and research environment have continually evolved, often accompanied by controversial opinions about new methodologies. In this paper, we embrace this change by introducing a new approach to qualitative analysis in HCI using Large Language Models (LLMs).

arxiv-2407-08943.title: A Deployable Quantum Access Points Selection Algorithm for Large-Scale Localization
arxiv-2407-08943.creator: Ahmed Shokry, Moustafa youssef
arxiv-2407-08943.description: Abstract Effective access points (APs) selection is a crucial step in localization systems. It directly affects both localization accuracy and computational efficiency. Classical APs selection algorithms are usually computationally expensive, hindering the deployment of localization systems in a large worldwide scale. In this paper, we introduce a quantum APs selection algorithm for large-scale localization systems.

arxiv-2411-08137.title: New matrices for spectral hypergraph theory, II
arxiv-2411-08137.creator: R. Vishnupriya, R. Rajkumar
arxiv-2411-08137.description: Abstract The properties of a hypergraph explored through the spectrum of its unified matrix was made by the authors in [ 26 ] . In this paper, we introduce three different hypergraph matrices: unified Laplacian matrix, unified signless Laplacian matrix, and unified normalized Laplacian matrix, all defined using the unified matrix.

arxiv-2510-03165.title: FTTE: Federated Learning on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices
arxiv-2510-03165.creator: Irene Tenison, Anna Murphy, Charles Beauville, Lalana Kagal
arxiv-2510-03165.description: Abstract Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices while preserving data privacy, but deployment on resource-constrained edge nodes remains challenging due to limited memory, energy, and communication bandwidth. Traditional synchronous and asynchronous FL approaches further suffer from straggler-induced delays and slow convergence in heterogeneous, large-scale networks.

arxiv-2601-21252.title: Lossless Copyright Protection via Intrinsic Model Fingerprinting
arxiv-2601-21252.creator: Lingxiao Chen, Liqin Wang, Wei Lu, Xiangyang Luo
arxiv-2601-21252.description: Abstract The exceptional performance of diffusion models establishes them as high-value intellectual property but exposes them to unauthorized replication. Existing protection methods either modify the model to embed watermarks, which impairs performance, or extract model fingerprints by manipulating the denoising process, rendering them incompatible with black-box APIs.

pmc-13595340.title: Cryptochrome-mediated integration of circadian rhythms into seasonal cycles in the silkworm Bombyx mori
pmc-13595340.creator: Daniel J. Brady, Federica Sandrelli
pmc-13595340.description: The domesticated silkworm Bombyx mori is both a major sericultural species and a powerful model for studying how environmental cues are converted into developmental decisions.
